title: What is Hyperlocal Marketing? Strategies, Tools & Real-World Examples

facts.fact: Google data cited by the page states that local searches without the phrase 'near me' are growing 150% faster than those that include it.
facts.quote: Local searches _without_ the phrase “near me” are now growing**[**150% faster**](https://www.thinkwithgoogle.com/marketing-strategies/app-and-mobile/local-search-mobile-search-micro-moments/) than those that include it.

facts.fact: According to Google, 60% of mobile users contact a business directly from search results.
facts.quote: According to Google, [**60% of mobile users**](https://www.thinkwithgoogle.com/marketing-strategies/app-and-mobile/smartphone-user-search-behavior-statistics/)**contact a business directly from search results.**

facts.fact: The page cites McKinsey stating that 71% of consumers prefer brands that give them personalized experiences.
facts.quote: And it works: [**71% of consumers prefer**](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/the-value-of-getting-personalization-right-or-wrong-is-multiplying) brands that give them personalized experiences.

facts.fact: The page describes hyperlocal marketing as focusing on a tight radius sometimes as small as 100 to 500 meters around a store or event, compared with zip code or citywide targeting for traditional local marketing.
facts.quote: sometimes as small as 100 to 500 meters around a store or event.

facts.fact: The page's comparison table lists the specific radius for hyperlocal marketing as 100–500m.
facts.quote: | **Target Area** | City, zip code, region | Specific radius (e.g. 100–500m) |

facts.fact: The page gives an example of a hyperlocal offer sent to someone walking within 100 meters of a store.
facts.quote: Send a special offer to someone walking within 100 meters of your store

facts.fact: Marketers can set a geofence radius as small as 50 meters or as wide as a few miles, depending on the campaign goal.
facts.quote: Marketers can set the radius to be as small as 50 meters or as wide as a few miles, depending on the goal.

facts.fact: Geofencing uses GPS, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth to create a virtual boundary around a physical location, and entering that area can trigger an action such as a text, push notification, or mobile ad.
facts.quote: uses GPS, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth to create a virtual boundary around a physical location.

facts.fact: Google Ads, Meta Ads, and GroundTruth are named by the vendor as advertising platforms that already use AI-driven optimization behind the scenes.
facts.quote: Most advertising platforms like Google Ads, Meta Ads, and GroundTruth already use AI-driven optimization behind the scenes.

facts.fact: Small businesses can start with AR using user-friendly platforms named as Instagram Spark AR, ZapWorks, or BlippAR.
facts.quote: Even small businesses can get started with AR using user-friendly platforms like Instagram Spark AR, ZapWorks, or BlippAR.

facts.fact: Local behavior data for hyperlocal targeting can be gathered from tools named as Google Analytics, Meta Local Insights, Foursquare, and GroundTruth.
facts.quote: You can gather these insights from tools like **Google Analytics** (with location-based goals), **Meta Local Insights**, or platforms like **Foursquare** and **GroundTruth**

facts.fact: Geo Targetly describes its browser-based tools (Geo Popups, Geo Bars, Geo Redirect) as able to deliver location-triggered experiences even without a mobile app.
facts.quote: even without a mobile app, **browser-based tools like Geo Targetly** can deliver location-triggered experiences effectively.

facts.fact: Burger King's 2018 "Whopper Detour" campaign geofenced a 600-foot area around McDonald's locations in the U.S.
facts.quote: They geofenced a 600-foot area around McDonald’s locations in the U.S.

facts.fact: In Burger King's 2018 "Whopper Detour" campaign, app users near a McDonald's were offered a Whopper for one cent.
facts.quote: they’d receive an offer for a Whopper for just one cent.

facts.fact: Burger King's "Whopper Detour" campaign was reported to have led over 1 million people to download the Burger King app within days.
facts.quote: the app within days, and it shot to #1 in the App Store.

facts.fact: Geofencing is defined on the page as setting up a virtual boundary around a specific location and triggering ads or messages when someone enters that area.
facts.quote: Set up a virtual boundary around a specific location

facts.fact: The American Red Cross campaign drew more than 600 extra donors to local donation sites during the campaign, according to the cited GroundTruth case study.
facts.quote: The result? More than [600 extra donors visited](https://www.groundtruth.com/insight/american-red-cross/

facts.fact: Stores using hyperlocal ads typically reach people within a short distance of about 0.5 to 2 miles.
facts.quote: Stores use hyperlocal ads to reach people within a short distance, like 0.5 to 2 miles.

facts.fact: Curry's PC World, in the UK, reported a 12.4% jump in store visits after using mobile ads near its stores, per the cited GroundTruth case study.
facts.quote: In the UK, Curry’s PC World used mobile ads near their stores and saw a [12.4% jump in visits]

facts.fact: A campaign for an organic energy drink using location-based ads near stores saw a 583% boost in traffic to those locations, per the cited GroundTruth case study.
facts.quote: saw a[583% boost in traffic](https://www.groundtruth.com/insight/yachak-mate-organic-energy-tea/)

facts.fact: Geo Targetly's paid plan starts at $9 per month when billed yearly, and a free trial is available.
facts.quote: Free trial available; paid plan starts at [$9/month billed yearly]

facts.fact: GroundTruth pricing is custom based on campaign size and is typically suited for businesses spending $1,000+ per month on ads.
facts.quote: Typically suited for businesses spending **$1,000+/month on ads.**

facts.fact: Meta local ads pricing can start at $5 per day, with performance depending on audience size, competition, and creative quality.
facts.quote: Flexible can start with **as little as $5/day**.

facts.fact: Google Ads location-targeted pay-per-click campaigns can start at $10–$50 per day, and competitive industries may need higher budgets.
facts.quote: You can start with **$10–$50/day**, but competitive industries may require higher budgets.

facts.fact: Google Ads location targeting can show ads within a radius of as small as 1 km.
facts.quote: down to a 1 km radius

facts.fact: Meta Local Ads radius targeting is limited to a minimum of 1 mile, according to the comparison table.
facts.quote: Radius targeting limited (1-mile min)

facts.fact: Foursquare Studio offers a free tier, with pro features available at additional cost; Foursquare Ads pricing is custom.
facts.quote: Studio offers a free tier, with pro features available at additional cost.

facts.fact: Geo Targetly describes its geo-personalization as working down to city and zip code level based on visitor location.
facts.quote: down to city and zip code level

facts.fact: A Geo Targetly blog page cites recent studies, via a third-party market report, showing a 45% increase in customer engagement from in-store Bluetooth beacon interactions.
facts.quote: with recent studies showing a [45% increase](https://www.globalgrowthinsights.com/market-reports/bluetooth-beacon-and-ibeacon-market-108433) in customer engagement

facts.fact: A Geo Targetly blog page cites recent studies showing a 35% rise in conversions from in-store beacon interactions.
facts.quote: in customer engagement and a 35% rise in conversions from in-store beacon interactions

facts.fact: The page states that Target uses Bluetooth beacons that send personalized deals to a customer's phone when the customer walks into the store.
facts.quote: Stores like Target are already using Bluetooth beacons that ping a customer’s phone with personalized deals the moment they walk in.

facts.fact: Studies cited by the page show that product recommendations tailored to individual users can boost website conversion rates by as much as 49% (third-party claim from Fresh Relevance).
facts.quote: studies show that product recommendations tailored to individual users can boost website conversion rates by as much as

facts.fact: The page states that over half of all consumers say they have used voice to search for things like nearby stores or business hours.
facts.quote: over half of all consumers say they’ve used voice to search for things like nearby stores or business hours

facts.fact: The page recommends a targeting radius of 100 meters to 1 mile for foot-traffic businesses such as restaurants, cafés, clinics, or retail stores.
facts.quote: a range between 100 meters and 1 mile works well for foot traffic-based businesses like restaurants, cafés, clinics, or retail stores

facts.fact: The page suggests a slightly wider radius of 1–5 miles for services such as real estate or event venues.
facts.quote: For services like real estate or event venues, a slightly wider radius (1–5 miles) might be more effective.

facts.fact: The page states hyperlocal campaigns can start with budgets as low as $5–10 per day using Google Ads or Meta Ads.
facts.quote: You can start with budgets as low as $5–10 per day using tools like Google Ads or Meta Ads.
